summary: Orders Web lets customer-service agents find a customer's orders, look at one order with its lines, and get the current price from the central pricing service while the customer is on the phone. A monthly database clean-up cancels orders left pending for more than six months.

domains.name: Order servicing
domains.description: Answering customers' questions about their orders.

capabilities.name: Sign in
capabilities.description: Agents sign in with their user name and password before using the application.

capabilities.name: Find orders
capabilities.description: Search orders by customer and status.

capabilities.name: View and price an order
capabilities.description: Show one order with its lines and its price including tax, confirmed by the pricing service.

capabilities.name: Cancel stale orders
capabilities.description: Orders pending for more than six months are cancelled by a SQL script.

actors.name: Pricing service
actors.description: Central service that returns the current price of an order.

actors.name: Database administrator
actors.description: Runs the deployment and clean-up scripts.

use_cases.name: Sign in
use_cases.goal: Get access to the order screens
steps: See the order search screen, or the error page when the password is wrong

use_cases.name: Find a customer's orders
use_cases.goal: See the orders of the customer on the phone
steps: Type the customer and optionally a status
Read the list of matching orders

use_cases.name: View an order with its price
use_cases.goal: Answer a question about one order and its price
steps: Click an order in the list
Read its lines and the price including tax
use_cases.outcome: The order detail with a current price.

business_rules.name: Only known users can sign in
business_rules.description: When the user name and password do not match a known user, the agent is sent to the error page instead of the order screens.

business_rules.name: Price includes tax and is confirmed centrally
business_rules.description: The order total is computed with tax in the database, then confirmed by the pricing service before it is shown.

business_rules.name: Pending orders expire after six months
business_rules.description: When an order has been pending for more than six months, its status becomes CANCELLED.

data_entities.name: Customer
data_entities.description: A person or company that places orders.

data_entities.name: Order
data_entities.description: An order with its status and creation date.

data_entities.name: Order line
data_entities.description: One product and quantity on an order.

data_entities.name: Application user
data_entities.description: An agent allowed to sign in.

screens.next_steps: On success the order search screen opens; on failure the error page.

screens.purpose: The agent finds the orders of a customer.
screens.data_shown: Orders with customer, status and date.
screens.next_steps: Opening an order shows its detail.

screens.purpose: The agent reads one order and its price.
screens.data_shown: Order header, lines and the price including tax.
screens.next_steps: Back to the search for the next question.

screens.purpose: Tells the agent something went wrong, for example a wrong password.

interfaces.purpose: Confirms the current price of an order.
interfaces.data_exchanged: Order number and local total out; confirmed price back.

glossary.meaning: A customer-service employee who uses Orders Web.
An order that is not yet confirmed or shipped.
